title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the General Provisions of the Contract Part of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en:
Article 61 Where, in a periodic contract with continuous performance obligations, one party fails to perform monetary debts such as payment of price or rent, and the other party requests dissolution of the contract, the People's Court, upon trial finding that the contract should be dissolved according to law, may, based on the claims of the parties and taking into account factors such as the contract parties, type of transaction, changes in market prices, and remaining performance period, determine the reasonable period for the non-breaching party to find an alternative transaction, and determine the benefits obtainable after performance of the contract by deducting the corresponding performance costs payable by the non-breaching party from the price or rent corresponding to such period.
Where the non-breaching party claims that the benefits obtainable after performance of the contract should be determined by deducting the performance costs from the price or rent corresponding to the remaining performance period after dissolution of the contract, the People's Court shall not support such claim, except where the remaining performance period is shorter than the reasonable period for finding an alternative transaction.

Article 62 Where the benefits obtainable by the non-breaching party after performance of the contract cannot be determined pursuant to Articles 60 and 61 of this Interpretation, the People's Court may, taking into comprehensive consideration factors such as the benefits gained by the breaching party from the breach, the degree of fault of the breaching party, and other circumstances of the breach, determine such benefits in accordance with the principles of fairness and good faith.

Article 63 In determining the 'loss that the breaching party foresaw or ought to have foreseen at the time of concluding the contract as a possible consequence of the breach' as provided in Article 584 of the Civil Code, the People's Court shall, based on the purpose of the contract concluded by the parties and taking into comprehensive consideration factors such as the contract parties, contract content, type of transaction, trade practices, and negotiation process, determine such loss in accordance with what a civil subject in the same or similar situation as the breaching party would have foreseen or ought to have foreseen at the time of concluding the contract.
Where the non-breaching party claims that, in addition to the benefits obtainable after performance of the contract, there are other losses caused by the breach, such as additional expenses payable by the non-breaching party for bearing liability for breach of contract to a third party, and requests the breaching party to compensate for such losses, and upon trial it is found that such losses were foreseen or ought to have been foreseen by the breaching party at the time of concluding the contract, the People's Court shall support such claim.
In determining the amount of damages for breach of contract, where the breaching party claims to deduct the losses increased due to the non-breaching party's failure to take appropriate measures, the corresponding losses caused by the fault of the non-breaching party, or the additional benefits obtained or necessary expenses reduced by the non-breaching party due to the breach, the People's Court shall support such claims in accordance with law.

Article 64 Where a party requests adjustment of liquidated damages by way of a counterclaim or defense, the People's Court shall support such request in accordance with law.
Where the breaching party claims that the agreed liquidated damages are excessively higher than the losses caused by the breach and requests an appropriate reduction, such party shall bear the burden of adducing evidence. Where the non-breaching party claims that the agreed liquidated damages are reasonable, such party shall also provide corresponding evidence.
Where a party merely claims that the agreed liquidated damages shall not be adjusted on the ground that the contract stipulates that the liquidated damages may not be adjusted, the People's Court shall not support such claim.

Article 65 Where a party claims that the agreed liquidated damages are excessively higher than the losses caused by the breach and requests an appropriate reduction, the People's Court shall, based on the losses as provided in Article 584 of the Civil Code, taking into account factors such as the contract parties, type of transaction, performance of the contract, degree of fault of the parties, and background of performance, measure in accordance with the principles of fairness and good faith, and render a judgment.
Where the agreed liquidated damages exceed 30% of the losses caused, the People's Court may generally determine that the liquidated damages are excessively higher than the losses caused.
Where a party that has acted in bad faith in committing the breach requests a reduction of the liquidated damages, the People's Court shall generally not support such request.

Article 66 Where one party requests the other party to pay liquidated damages, and the other party defends on the grounds that the contract is not established, void, revoked, determined to have no legal effect, does not constitute a breach, or the non-breaching party has sustained no loss, without claiming an adjustment to the excessively high liquidated damages, the People's Court shall clarify whether the party requests adjustment to the liquidated damages if such defense is not upheld. Where the first-instance People's Court finds the defense established and fails to clarify, and the second-instance People's Court finds that a judgment for payment of liquidated damages should be rendered, it may directly clarify, and based on the party's request, after the parties have fully adduced evidence, conducted cross-examination, and debated on whether the liquidated damages should be adjusted, render a judgment for an appropriate reduction of liquidated damages in accordance with law.
Where the defendant, due to objective reasons, did not appear in court in the first-instance proceedings but appears in court in the second-instance proceedings and requests a reduction of the liquidated damages, the second-instance People's Court may, after the parties have fully adduced evidence, conducted cross-examination, and debated on whether the liquidated damages should be adjusted, render a judgment for an appropriate reduction of the liquidated damages in accordance with law.

Article 67 Where a party delivers a retention deposit, guarantee deposit, security deposit, bargaining deposit, earnest money, or booking deposit, etc., without stipulating the nature of earnest money, and one party requests application of the earnest money penalty rule provided in Article 587 of the Civil Code, the People's Court shall not support such request. Where the parties stipulate the nature of earnest money but do not specify the type of earnest money or the specification is unclear, and one party claims it as earnest money for breach, the People's Court shall support such claim.
Where the parties agree that the delivery of earnest money shall serve as security for concluding the contract, and one party refuses to conclude the contract or, in breach of the principle of good faith during negotiation of the contract, causes the contract not to be concluded, and the other party requests application of the earnest money penalty rule provided in Article 587 of the Civil Code, the People's Court shall support such request.
Where the parties agree that the delivery of earnest money shall be a condition for the formation or effectiveness of the contract, and the party who should deliver the earnest money fails to do so, but the principal obligations under the contract have been fully performed and accepted by the other party, the People's Court shall find that the contract was formed or became effective at the time the other party accepted such performance.
Where the parties agree that the earnest money is of a rescission nature, and the party delivering the earnest money claims to rescind the contract at the cost of forfeiting the earnest money, or the party receiving the earnest money claims to rescind the contract at the cost of returning double the earnest money, the People's Court shall support such claim.

Article 68 Where both parties have breaching acts that cause the purpose of the contract to be unattainable, and one party requests application of the earnest money penalty rule, the People's Court shall not support such request. Where one party has only a minor breach, and the other party has a breaching act that causes the purpose of the contract to be unattainable, and the party with a minor breach claims application of the earnest money penalty rule, and the other party defends on the ground that the party with a minor breach also constitutes a breach, the People's Court shall not support such defense.
Where one party has partially performed the contract, and the other party accepts such performance and requests application of the earnest money penalty rule in proportion to the unperformed portion, the People's Court shall support such request. Where the other party requests application of the earnest money penalty rule with respect to the entire contract, the People's Court shall not support such request, except where the partial non-performance causes the purpose of the contract to be unattainable.
Where the contract cannot be performed due to force majeure, and the non-breaching party requests application of the earnest money penalty rule, the People's Court shall not support such request.
IX. Supplementary Provisions

Article 69 This Interpretation shall come into force as of December 5, 2023.
For civil cases arising from legal facts after the entry into force of the Civil Code that have not yet been finally adjudicated before the entry into force of this Interpretation, this Interpretation shall apply; for civil cases that have been finally adjudicated before the entry into force of this Interpretation, where a party applies for a retrial or a retrial is decided pursuant to the trial supervision procedure, this Interpretation shall not apply.
